narrative.text: Justin 2026-08-07, mid-flight on the LIVE promo: 'just make the One time purchasers get 30% off too.' d=20 -> 24, fsd=10 -> 15. Renders 30-31% OTP / 34% subs across every markup in scope. WHY d=24 AND NOT 23: d=23 renders only 29% on the thinner markups (11oz-class 1.0883, 500g 1.0910) and would print BELOW the 30% claim. d=24 renders 30.17%-30.91% -- never under. WHY fsd HAD TO MOVE IN THE SAME BREATH: at d=24/fsd=10 the lanes INVERT -- one-time buyers pay 0.7600 of price while first-subscription buyers pay 0.7650, so a subscriber would pay MORE than a one-time buyer. That violates Justin's own standing subs-always-deeper rule (2026-08-06) and nothing in the stack would have flagged it. At fsd=15 subs pay 0.7225 vs 0.7600 -- genuinely deeper, and 4 points clear on the rendered basis (34% vs 30%). THE UNDERLYING JUSTIFICATION: the Fri Aug 7 launch email already advertises 30%, which at d=20 was true ONLY for subscribers. The declaration had carried this as an OPEN accuracy risk ('an unqualified 30% OFF Bulk Bags headline remains false for a one-time buyer at 20%'). This change makes the sent copy true rather than requiring the copy to be qualified after the fact. MAP: CLEAR. Bulk (5lb/500g) carries no MSRP and no MAP at all; all six 50 ct teas are map=NULL. Nothing in scope is among the 77 MAP items, so no CatalogSmith gate. SUPERSEDES THE MOCHA EXCEPTION: at d=24 SKU 40086 renders 30.17% unaided, so the per-variant d=21 node becomes unnecessary and must be cancelled rather than left orphaned in the teardown. STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE, FLAGGED ONCE: this makes a 72-hour August MINOR the deepest promo of 2026 at 30% displayed, five points deeper than BFCM's current d=18 (25% displayed). Re-rate BFCM when November creative is briefed or it ships looking weaker than an August flash sale.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE 2026-08-07 by Shopkeeper. 60 metafield writes, 0 userErrors, both legs together. NODES: OTP 1563704852728 = 0.24 ACTIVE; SUB 1563704885496 = 0.15 ACTIVE; both endsAt 2026-08-10T06:59:59Z, both 30 variants, lane flags correct (OTP node OTP=True/Sub=False, SUB node OTP=False/Sub=True). METAFIELDS: 30/30 at custom.discount=24 AND 30/30 at custom.first_subscription_discount=15 -- a count, not a sample. MOCHA EXCEPTION NODE NEVER EXISTED: paginated 77-node census shows variant 47363729752312 contained by exactly two nodes, the two Bulk Bag Sale nodes. The only other name-match, 1415847182584 'Mocha One Time x3', is EXPIRED and does not contain the variant. No orphan. FOTM UNTOUCHED: 9/9 at 20/10 across all four products including 40116; verified disjoint from promo scope BEFORE writing, so no stacking. SERVED HTML: 60030 (5lb, markup 1.1000) 'Bulk Bag Sale - Save 31%', $68.40; 80066A (500g, 1.0910) 'Save 30%', $16.72; 40086 (Mocha, 1.0883) 'Save 30%' on section render; sub pill uniform '34% OFF First Shipment - then 15% off recurring' across all. 40116 control still reads 'Flavor of the Month - Save 27% - Ends August 31'. RENDER SPREAD, ACCEPTED: 4 variants render 30% and 26 render 31%. Never below the 30% claim, so the never-show-less-than-promised guardrail holds; the site simply over-delivers on the thicker markups. Sub pill is uniform 34%. MOCHA PAGE-CACHE LAG, BENIGN: 40086's cached PDP briefly served 26%/$13.60 while its section render showed 30%. Cause identified -- the page was warmed by a pre-write fetch during sub-pill discovery. 14 attempts with distinct &cb= params all returned stale, confirming query params do NOT bust Shopify's page cache; only TTL does. Lag direction is the SAFE one (stale page UNDERSTATES at 26% while the cart charges 30% off compare-at) -- which is precisely why the nodes-first write order was chosen. TEARDOWN RE-PROVEN, no code change needed: --if-needed trips on `d not in ('0', None)` and is value-agnostic, so 24/15 needs no update; the only hard-coded 20/10 are the FOTM control assertions, which stay correct because FOTM stays at 20/10. MECHANIC: discountAutomaticBasicUpdate -> customerGets.items.products.productVariantsToAdd. NO tagging, NO collection write. THE VARIANT-ISOLATION PROBLEM I ESCALATED DID NOT EXIST: both Bulk Bag Sale nodes were ALREADY variant-scoped (DiscountProducts with an explicit productVariants list, products[]=0) and never referenced collection 486918029560 at all -- that smart collection is a decoupled landing surface, so the 10ct/25ct siblings are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a drift-prone rule. Nodes 1563704852728 (OTP 0.2) and 1563704885496 (SUB 0.1) each went 26 -> 30 variants. All four new 50 ct variants present in both; 40116 and 43116 absent from both; zero 10ct/25ct siblings in either. Per-variant metafields now 20/10 on 40016 (46160189522168), 40066 (45167436464376), 40086 (47363729752312), 43226 (45354354835704); 43116 (46160227827960) untouched at 0/0; 40116 (45275234140408) untouched at its pre-existing FOTM 20/10. ENDSAT: my brief's endsAt=null premise was STALE -- both bulk nodes already carried 2026-08-10T06:59:59Z (= Aug 9 11:59:59 PM PDT) and were correct; nothing changed. The only null-endsAt nodes store-wide are the two FOTM nodes, perpetual by design. STACKING HAZARD CONFIRMED, and it retroactively justifies leaving 40116 alone: product 6681928892585 carries tag FOTM and sits in collection 405982150904; the FOTM nodes are COLLECTION-scoped and all four nodes have combinesWith.productDiscounts=true, so adding 40116 to a bulk node would have STACKED to ~36% OTP / ~19% SUB. Its metafields already read 20/10 so its pill renders identically with no action. The four target parents are NOT in the FOTM collection. PROCESS: an unpaginated automaticDiscountNodes(first:60) MISSED both Bulk nodes -- the store has 77 automatic nodes; always paginate. | PRIOR STATE: BUILT AND LAUNCHING at d=20/fsd=10 (renders 27%/30%) -- ARMED 2026-08-06, collection 486918029560, nodes 1563704852728 + 1563704885496. DELIBERATELY LEFT at the old rate: it goes live at 00:00 Aug 7 with an email already scheduled, so it is the one exception to the new 20/30 standard. | Pairs with the 'Bulk Bags for More Savings' email at August!G23 = Fri Aug 7 (the launch day; the old 'Aug 8' in this note was wrong). Fills the month's weakest week (Aug 3-9 2025: 652 orders, $43.78 AOV). SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-07 BY JUSTIN, MID-FLIGHT: the 50 ct tagless teas ARE in scope and were wrongly dropped. | RETRACTED -- the 2026-08-06 decision read: 'workbook D5's header listed 5Lb/500g/50ct Tagless while its own SCOPE line said 5lb only. 50ct tagless is 1 eligible product (rest are TARGET listings + a demo), so it is dropped -- a 1-product format reads as a broken promise in the email.' THAT COUNT WAS WRONG. The sellable 50 ct is a VARIANT on each parent tea product (beside 10ct and 25ct), not a standalone product; I enumerated standalone listings, found only the unpublished TARGET ones, and concluded the format was empty. Verified at source 2026-08-07: SIX 50 ct items exist -- 40016 (Vanilla Nut - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 287), 40066 (Hazelnut - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 21), 40086 (Mocha - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 80), 40116 (French Roast - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 45), 43116 (Dandelion Dark Roast - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 0), 43226 (Dandelion Caramel Nut - Herbal Tea - 50 ct, inv 344). MAP: all six carry map=NULL in the product master -- NOT among the 77 MAP items, so no CatalogSmith gate. LESSON: when counting a FORMAT (50ct, 10oz, 5lb), enumerate VARIANTS, never products -- a format that exists only as variant 3 of a multi-variant product is invisible to a product-level count. 5lb=22 + 500g=6 + 50ct=5. Needs a purpose-built collection: the existing '5lb Bag Herbal Coffee' smart collection holds 0 products (conjunctive rules on TAG '5 lb bag' AND '5 lb grind'; the real tag is '5lb ground'). fsd is 10 and STAYS 10. The storefront sub pill computes (compare_at - price*0.85*(1-fsd/100))/compare_at, so fsd=10 renders 30% OFF First Shipment across every markup in scope (5lb 1.1000 -> 30.4%; 500g 1.0910 -> 29.9%; both round to 30). The email's '30% OFF' claim is therefore TRUE for subscribers as built, with no rate change. RETRACTED 2026-08-06: an earlier pass on this same day raised fsd 10->18 on the argument that fsd=10 'delivered only 23.5%' and that claims are measured off `price`. That premise was WRONG -- the theme divides by compare_at, not price -- and the raise was REVERTED the same day with Justin's approval. Shopkeeper reverted the build script to fsd=10 and re-synced the promo-hub feeds (11/11 declared promos matching, 0 mismatches). DO NOT treat any part of that reasoning as an argument to re-raise fsd; ThemeSmith's promo-rendering-model.md is authoritative on where the claim is rendered. OPEN: an unqualified '30% OFF Bulk Bags' headline remains false for a one-time buyer at 20% -- copy must tie 30% to subscribing. Two nodes required: 'Bulk Bag Sale OTP' + 'Bulk Bag Sale SUB'.

decisions.question: Remaining cross-lane defect: subscription line loses its discount in a mixed cart
decisions.decision: Justin: 'I DONT CARE IF THE DISCOUNT AMOUNTS ARE DIFFERENT. JUST MAKE SURE THEY BOTH GIVE DISCOUNTS. JUST PUT THEM ALL ON THE SUMMER WELLNESS SALE. AT THE END OF THE WELLNESS SALE REIMPLEMENT THE FOTM FOR ALL FRENCH ROAST SKUS.' Supersedes my recommendation to defer the subscription fix to the next promo. Guaranteeing a discount on every line outranks preserving the deeper 20% FOTM rate for the final 13 hours.
decisions.orderingConstraint: FOTM nodes MUST be deactivated BEFORE custom.discount is written to 18. Doing it in the other order puts French Roast in BOTH 'Flavor of the Month' and 'Discount = 18' while both node sets are combinable, which STACKS FOTM 20% on top of Wellness 18% (~38% off). The chosen order risks only a brief window where French Roast is under-discounted, which is recoverable; a double discount is not.

decisions.question: Re-plan after Shopkeeper's dispatch died on an upstream 529 with 15 tool calls executed
decisions.decision: Verified at source that NOTHING landed: all 4 nodes in their prior state, all 9 variants still 20/10, zero FOTM handles in Discount = 18, no double-discount exposure. Replaced the 3-step plan (9 metafield writes + 2 deactivations + 1 flip) with a 2-node-change plan that reaches the same outcome.
decisions.whyBetter: Strictly safer on four counts: (a) no bulk metafield write, so nothing to restore -- teardown drops from 11 operations to 1; (b) FAILURE-SAFE ordering -- if it dies after step 1, French Roast subscriptions are still covered by Wellness SUB at the same 10%, whereas the old plan's step 1 left French Roast with NO discount until step 2 completed; (c) no intermediate state can produce the ~38% double discount; (d) French Roast keeps its deeper 20% one-time rate, so no advertised claim changes. Justin's requirement was 'JUST MAKE SURE THEY BOTH GIVE DISCOUNTS' and he explicitly accepted differing amounts, so a deeper rate under the already-unified 'Summer Wellness Sale' label satisfies it.

narrative.text: *** RE-RATED MID-FLIGHT ON A LIVE PROMO, ON JUSTIN'S ORDER. d=13 -> d=18. fsd STAYS 10. *** Justin, #promosmith 2026-08-13, hours after launch: 'wtf all the OTP products should be at least 25% OFF. This is no different than most of the other sales we've ran. The subs need to say 30% off. get this done right.' He is the authorised decider on a live promo and this is that authorisation. ARITHMETIC VERIFIED AGAINST THE RENDERER BEFORE ANY WRITE, not assumed: badge = round(100*(1-(1-d/100)/m)), sub pill = round(100*(1-0.85*(1-fsd/100)/m)) where m = compare_at/price. Across the four real markups (11oz 1.0883 thinnest, 500g 1.0910, 5lb 1.1000, 10oz 1.1053): d=18 renders 24.65%-25.81% and DISPLAYS 25%-26%; fsd=10 renders 29.71%-30.79% and DISPLAYS 30%-31%. So d=18/fsd=10 delivers exactly what Justin asked for. THE SUBS LEG NEEDED NO CHANGE -- fsd=10 already displayed 30%; only the OTP leg was short. Resisted the reflex to raise fsd 'to match the 30% ask', which would have been the recurring expensive error (fsd is the INCREMENT on Stay.ai's 15%, never the marketing percentage). SUBS-DEEPER GUARDRAIL RE-CHECKED AND CLEAR: one-time pays 0.8200 of price, first-subscription pays 0.85*0.90 = 0.7650, so subs are genuinely deeper by 0.0550 and the displayed gap is a uniform 5 points on EVERY size class -- no tie, unlike the BFCM 23/10 defect. Minimum fsd required at d=18 is 3.53; fsd=10 clears with room. NOT A NEW DEPTH: d=18/fsd=10 is the pre-2026-08-06 standard and the same pair declared for BFCM, so it introduces no new MAP exposure beyond the standing (and still open) price==MSRP==MAP item. THE MECHANICAL TRAP THAT MAKES THIS FOUR CHANGES AND NOT ONE: both nodes are COLLECTION-scoped on smart collection 487085441272 'Discount = 13', whose rule is custom.discount == 13. Sweeping variants to 18 drops them OUT of the very collection the nodes read, so a naive metafield sweep silently un-discounts a live sitewide sale. Required: (a) declaredSlate d=13 -> 18 BEFORE anything runs, or Shopkeeper's assert_no_rate_drift SystemExits; (b) OTP node 1564613083384 0.13 -> 0.18; (c) node scope must cover custom.discount==18 with membership CONTINUOUS through the transition; (d) sweep 264 variants 13 -> 18. SUB node 1564613116152 and every fsd value are UNTOUCHED. SAFE ORDER, and it follows the same principle as the original nodes-first launch: raise the NODE percentage before sweeping the metafields. Between those steps the cart over-delivers (18% off) while the badge still reads 20% off the old metafield -- understating, which is the safe direction. Sweeping first would have under-delivered against a live 20-25% claim. FOTM CARVE-OUT SURVIVES BUT ITS MARGIN NARROWS: FOTM stays at d=20, which renders 26.49%-27.62% and displays 26%-28% -- still DEEPER than sitewide 25%-26% on every size class, so the label-precedence decision (FOTM wins because its rate is deeper) still holds. But on the thinnest 11oz markup the gap is now only 1 point (FOTM 26% vs sitewide 25%) where it used to be 6. If sitewide ever goes deeper than FOTM the whole carve-out rationale inverts and French Roast would need rescoping, not relabelling. FORWARD QUESTION FLAGGED ONCE, NOT ACTED ON: Justin's 'this is no different than most of the other sales we've ran' reads as the STANDARD reverting to 25%/30%, not a one-off for August. If so, Sept/Oct/Dec majors and all six minors still declared at d=13 need re-rating, and BFCM at d=18 would no longer be the year's deepest -- it would merely match a regular month. Not changing them in this pass; Justin asked for the live sale fixed, and re-rating five months is the planning work he explicitly stopped.

*** LAUNCHED EARLY ON JUSTIN'S DIRECT ORDER. Window is 2026-08-13..2026-08-20 = EIGHT DAYS, a deliberate one-off departure from the 7-day major rule. *** Justin, in #promosmith on 2026-08-13 at ~13:00 PT: 'I SAID LAUNCH IT NOW!' -- so the promo was pulled forward ~11 hours from its scheduled 23:45 PT node activation / 00:00 PT Aug 14 sweep and launched the same afternoon. Eight days of margin is the cheaper error. THREE WRITES WERE REQUIRED, NOT ONE, and this is the part most likely to be dropped by anyone repeating this: (1) startsAt moved to now on BOTH nodes 1564613083384 / 1564613116152; (2) campaign_sale_window_start moved 2026-08-14 -> 2026-08-13 on live theme 160800145656; (3) the sweep run immediately in the foreground instead of waiting for the 00:00 task. surfaces.launchEvidence: LIVE LABEL DEFECT, VERIFIED ON SERVED HTML BY PROMOSMITH 2026-08-28. Fetched the French Roast Instant Coffee PDP cache-busted: HTTP 200, 898,266 bytes, positive control OK (290 'Teeccino' occurrences, so the page really rendered). It shows the correct sale price 11.55, renders the label 'Flavor of the Month', and contains the string '72hr Instants Sale' ZERO times. So the CART IS RIGHT AND THE SIGN IS WRONG: the customer is charged the Instants-sale rate (30% off compare_at) under the name of a DIFFERENT promo that runs at 20% (27.3% off compare_at). Cause: 30008L/31008L carry the FOTM tag, and campaign_sale_window_exempt_tag='FOTM' deliberately exempts them from the campaign window label -- which was CORRECT while they were excluded from the sale, and became wrong the moment they were added to it. This is the 2026-08-06 mislabelled-sale defect in its exact original form: a pill naming the wrong promo. It is lower severity than a price error -- the customer is charged LESS than the label implies, not more -- but it is still a false statement on a live product page. @themesmith surface. It resolves automatically if Justin rules the two SKUs back OUT of the sale.

basis.v: d=23 DISPLAYS 29%-30% (29/29/30/30), fsd=15 DISPLAYS 34%-35%. Claim is the minimum displayed, so 29% and 34% -- DO NOT let creative round the OTP leg to '30% OFF': the 11oz and 500g classes print 29% and a 30% headline would overstate on them, which is an advertising-accuracy problem and MAP exposure on the 77 MAP items. Subs deeper by 0.0475 of price, +4 displayed. JUSTIN RATIFIED 2026-08-21 (Discord #promosmith, chose from a costed 4-option menu): majors 25% / minors 28% / BFCM 29% + 34% subs. Reconciles his 2026-08-13 order on the LIVE August sale ('all the OTP products should be at least 25% OFF ... This is no different than most of the other sales we've ran') with the 20% standard he had set himself on 08-06. The 20% figure did not survive contact and is now superseded. ALL RATES WITHIN SANCTIONED: d=18 is the pre-08-06 standard, d=23 at BFCM is rules.sanctionedException verbatim. ARITHMETIC VERIFIED AGAINST THE RENDERER, not assumed: badge=round(100*(1-(1-d/100)/m)), pill=round(100*(1-0.85*(1-fsd/100)/m)) across the four real markups (11oz 1.0883 thinnest, 500g 1.0910, 5lb 1.1000, 10oz 1.1053). Advertised claim = the MINIMUM DISPLAYED value across all four, never the raw rate and never rounded in our favour.

basis.v: d=22 DISPLAYS 28%-29% (28/29/29/29), fsd=15 DISPLAYS 34%-35%. Claim is the minimum displayed. Clears the new 25% major by +3 printed points on EVERY size class, which is the whole point of a narrow-scope minor. fsd RAISED 10 -> 15 BY DERIVATION, NOT BY ASK. Justin named the OTP outcome (28%); the subscription leg is mine to compute. At d=22/fsd=10 the sub pill prints only +1 point deeper than the OTP badge on the 500g and 5lb classes (OTP 28/29/29/29 vs SUB 30/30/30/31) -- subscribers get essentially nothing extra, which is the Feb-2026 5lb and BFCM 23/10 tie defect exactly. At fsd=15 the gap is +5 to +6 on every size class (SUB prints 34/34/34/35) and subs are deeper by 0.0575 of price. fsd=15 here is the subs-deeper guardrail doing its job -- it is NOT the marketing percentage mistaken for the increment.
